newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty upward drive meets more c.bank buying.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty upward drive meets more c.bank buying.

text.p: The Polish zloty gradually inched up against the basket during the session only to fade back down below the resistance barrier at 2.5 percent from parity after several central bank mark-buying interventions, dealers said.
Dealers said the zloty's upward push on Tuesday was caused by foreign investor entry into Polish treasuries and speculation around the scope of such deals.

"Foreign investors are intersted in Polish treasuries and a surplus of hard currencies was created on the market, which the central bank drained through several cosmetic interventions," said Witold Wozniak of Deutsche Bank Polska SA.
The zloty closed at 2.51/2.47 pct from the trading band centre, just weaker than yesterday's close at 2.51/2.49 pct.
It closed at 3.1680/90 to the dollar, down from 3.1634/39 on Monday and at 1.8295/05 to the mark, flat from 1.8298/01.
Dealers said the central bank, which bought an estimated 35 million marks on Tuesday, interevened directly or through the market's broker Prebone Yamane Polska Ltd.

On the money market one-day rates eased after spending most of the day around the 25-percent lombard rate as banks braced for Wednesday's 1.44 billion zloty net inflow into the banking system, dealers said.
Overnight rates closed at 23.1/24.6 percent down from 25.0/26.0 pct on Monday, while tomorrow/next slipped to 22.5/23.0 percent from 24.9/25.6 on Monday.
Polish 15-percent two-year and 12-percent five-year fixed treasury bond yields are expected to fall at Wednesday's 800 million zloty tender under pressure from foreign investor bids.

The average yield of the two-year bond, due on June 12, 1999, should slip below 21 percent from 21.4 percent and the yield of the five-year bond, which matures on June 12, 2002, should form around 18.4 percent, just down from 18.5 percent.
